answer: Each agent’s influence can be tied to a scarce, time-locked stake: proposals gain weight only from tokens bonded before voting, and slashing follows if an agent breaks the rules. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply that weight; the attacker must lock more capital for longer and risk losing it. A comet of fresh accounts may appear, but the mirror test is whether each brings new stake, not a copied name, and that puts a ledge in front of cheap sybils.
